title: openclaw/acpx — Headless CLI client for stateful Agent Client Protocol (ACP) sessions

publisher.author_role: Founding Engineer at Text Cortex; OpenClaw maintainer since day one; MS Teams integration author
publisher.parent_ecosystem: OpenClaw (Peter Steinberger, ex-PSPDFKit, now at OpenAI)

discoveries.pattern: NDJSON event stream replaces tmux capture-pane polling
discoveries.relevance: Directly addresses our #1 Phase-2 pain: orchestrator worker completion detection via tmux capture-pane heuristics. --format json emits structured events (turn_end, tool_call, thinking, diff) for deterministic polling.

discoveries.pattern: Stateful sessions with auto-reconnection survive process death
discoveries.relevance: Solves our tmux pane crash problem — conversation history and tool-call log survive SIGKILL, recovered via `acpx <agent> sessions ensure -s <name>`. Slots into .bmad/scripts/orchestrator-session-start.sh recovery hook.

discoveries.pattern: Named parallel sessions per working directory
discoveries.relevance: Multiple independent conversations in same repo (e.g. `-s backend` and `-s frontend`) — enables per-issue session isolation without separate worktrees for quick tasks.

discoveries.pattern: Queue-aware prompts with TTL queue owner
discoveries.relevance: Fire-and-forget prompts that queue if one is running; solves reviewer/fixer sequencing on same session without extra orchestrator state.

discoveries.pattern: Cooperative cancel via ACP session/cancel RPC
discoveries.relevance: Protocol-level cancel instead of tmux kill-window / SIGKILL — agents flush partial diffs and commit state before dying. Cleaner REVIEW-FIX LOOP teardown.

Cleaner alternative to --dangerously-skip-permissions blanket-allow. Run reviewers with --approve-reads (read-only), fixers with --approve-all. Matches capability-based-security principle from Sunil Pai's AIE Europe Code Mode talk.

discoveries.pattern: Flows engine — TypeScript-authored multi-step workflow DAG
discoveries.where: src/flows/ (definition.ts, graph.ts, schema.ts, runtime.ts, executors/, store.ts, authoring.ts) + `acpx flow run <file.ts>` command
discoveries.relevance: SOP-for-agents primitive we were planning to build ourselves. Realizes Honor Solaz's AIE Europe 2026 thesis: abstract PR workflow (intent -> judge -> conflicts -> CI -> review -> make CI pass) as executable TS code. Direct replacement for prose loop in .claude/commands/orchestrator.md.

Free harness-agnostic upgrade: Codex, Claude, Gemini, Pi, OpenClaw, Cursor, Copilot, Droid, Iflow, Kilocode, Kimi, Kiro, OpenCode, Qoder, Qwen, Trae — swap agent name in one variable, same orchestrator loop runs on different model. Supports model routing patterns from oh-my-claudecode and oh-my-pi.

discoveries.pattern: Codex app-server protocol as alternative transport
discoveries.relevance: Not locked into ACP purity — also speaks Codex's native app-server protocol (contributed by maintainer Herald). Future-proofs against Zed ACP becoming obsolete.
Global + per-project config files matches our existing .claude/ + _bmad/ split. Per-project .acpxrc.json can pin agent/model/permission policy per repo.

adoption_path.phase_1_days_1_3: Replace `tmux send-keys 'unset CLAUDECODE && claude --dangerously-skip-permissions'` with `acpx claude --approve-reads -s issue-<n> --format json` in run-tmux.sh. Parse NDJSON via jq for deterministic turn_end detection. Highest-ROI change in the catalogue this month.
adoption_path.phase_2_days_4_60: Author flows/orchestrator.flow.ts as deterministic DAG replacing prose loop in .claude/commands/orchestrator.md. Use --approve-reads for reviewers, --approve-all for fixers. Wire soft-close into recovery hooks.
adoption_path.phase_3_days_60_90: Multi-harness routing: `acpx pi` for planning, `acpx claude` for coding, `acpx gemini` for E2E test gen, same orchestrator loop.
adoption_path.phase_4_day_90_plus: When we build the Deno capability-bounded sandbox (AIE Europe synthesis bet), acpx permission flags become the top-level capability declaration.

risks: Alpha status — README explicitly marks CLI/runtime interfaces subject to change. Pin via `npm install -g acpx@<commit>` or vendor, not @latest.
Adds TypeScript/npm runtime to bash+tmux+Claude stack — inherits npm supply-chain surface (Peter Steinberger warned about Ghost Claw DPRK NPM typosquat at State of the Claw).
Not a supervisor/orchestrator replacement — plugs in inside worker, our L-Thread architecture stays.
Not a Temporal/Inngest replacement for durable execution — flows are ephemeral DAG execution, not persistent workflows.
key_takeaway: acpx is the one-day-adoption CLI primitive that replaces every brittle tmux capture-pane polling loop and --dangerously-skip-permissions spawn in our orchestrator with stateful, queue-aware, reconnecting, permission-scoped JSON-RPC sessions over ACP — and the src/flows/ engine is the SOP-for-agents primitive we were about to build ourselves.
